freebay.lead: A social commerce experience designed to bring discovery, relationships, and transactions into one system.
freebay.stateValue: Base implemented. Payments and media in hardening. Web planned.
freebay.summaryText: Marketplaces classify listings; social networks classify people. Freebay brings both together. Discovery starts from social context, passes through a traceable transaction, and keeps the conversation thread.
freebay.contextText: In a traditional classified service, the transaction is isolated and context is lost in chat. In a social network, context is abundant but reliable transactions are absent. Freebay treats discovery, relationships, and transactions as one system.
freebay.architectureText: The architecture separates clients, domain services, and external integrations so authentication, listings, payments, and notifications can evolve without making the interface own the rules.

freebay.chooseFlow: Choose discovery, conversation, or purchase. The diagram highlights the involved components and the steps show who decides each rule.

purchase.label: Purchase
purchase.title: Buy through an explainable transaction
purchase.description: Cart, order, payment, and delivery are separate states. Stripe stays isolated as an integration; payouts and refunds require hardening before production.
steps: Cart becomes an order grouped by seller
One payment is tracked per order
Delivery releases payout; dispute freezes it
Refund reverses and revokes digital access

freebayLabels.limitsTitle: What this study does not claim
freebayLabels.nonFunctional: Non-functional requirements: resource authorization, idempotent webhooks, money transitions recorded in an immutable ledger, and no capability marked ready before concurrency and replay testing.
freebayLabels.justification1: Local transactions and consistency while the domain is still moving; extract when a boundary stabilizes.
freebayLabels.justification2: Orders, payments, and entitlements require invariants and auditable referential integrity.
freebayLabels.justification3: Payouts, disputes, and refunds have their own lifecycle and cannot block the purchase.
freebayLabels.justification4: Chat and notifications need low latency; canonical state remains persisted in the domain.
freebayLabels.justification5: React and Flutter consume the same backend rules; divergence becomes a money bug.
freebayLabels.security1: DTO input validation at every HTTP boundary; the backend is authoritative for price, inventory, and order state.
freebayLabels.security2: Resource authorization: sellers, buyers, and mediators see only what their role permits.
freebayLabels.security3: Payment-provider webhooks are signature-verified and processed idempotently.
freebayLabels.security4: Paid media is served by an authorized endpoint; the current tolerance window is documented as hardening toward one-time signed URLs.
freebayLabels.verification1: Multi-seller checkout with one buyer payment and independent orders per seller, without an orphaned reservation.
freebayLabels.verification2: Webhook replay without duplicate debit or credit.
freebayLabels.verification3: Concurrent consumption of one-time credentials with exactly one winner.
freebayLabels.verification4: A refund that reverses the payout and revokes the corresponding digital access.
freebayLabels.verification5: No paid asset accessible through public URL enumeration.
freebayLabels.limitsText: There are no production metrics because there is no production: payouts, disputes, and one-time media remain in hardening, the web client is under construction, and domains still need to be acquired. The next steps, in this order and without shortcuts: complete the financial ledger with concurrency tests, close private-media authorization, build the web marketplace on the same contracts, and publish only then.
freebayLabels.resultText: The main result is a presentable full-stack foundation: the product can be read through its experience and through the structure that makes it possible, without invented metrics or promises beyond the evidence.
